description: Half of the second thing the bundle may ask of this shell: whether a system notification may be raised at all. Raising one is asked of this shell rather than of the plugin, because a click on a notification is answered by bringing the window forward and that answer is the shell's — `src/notifications.rs` hands the notification to the plugin's Rust side and answers the click it reports, and what the bundle calls is a command this application defines rather than a plugin's, so no capability names it. What is left here is the permission question, and it is two commands rather than the plugin's own default set, which also grants raising, scheduling, cancelling, listing what is pending or still on screen, and creating notification channels — the application asks for none of those. The platform list is deliberately narrower than the opener's beside it: Android is left off although the same library starts there, because a notification there needs the POST_NOTIFICATIONS runtime permission in the manifest and a channel to arrive on, which is #1616's work rather than something to grant by omission here; macOS is on the list for the reason it is on the opener's, that a contributor can build the desktop head there. A head this file does not name therefore refuses the command rather than answering it, and the application reads a refused command exactly as it reads an operating system that refused permission — the behaviour turns itself off on that device and asks again on none.
